newsitem.title: FRANCE: France urges U.N. to set up Zaire force quickly.
newsitem.headline: France urges U.N. to set up Zaire force quickly.

text.p: France urged the United Nations on Saturday to act as fast as possible to set up an international force to help refugees in Zaire and appealed to the United States to contribute a third of the troops.

Earlier, the Security Council had called on U.N. members to lay the groundwork for a force to help end the crisis threatening 1.2 million refugees, but it postponed its deployment until a later stage.
"This is an important step which we hope will lead as soon as possible to a new decision by the Security Council for its effective implementation," the French foreign ministry said in a statement.
It said later that France formally confirmed its proposal for a force of between 4,000 and 5,000 to U.N. Secretary General Boutros Boutros-Ghali on Saturday.

"The multinational force...should be made up of more or less equal parts by contingents from the United States, Africa and Europe," it said. "The deployment of this force should of course be aided by the states of the region concerned."

France and Spain have led calls this week to send a multinational force to help Hutu refugees threatened by a Tutsi uprising in eastern Zaire, where they fled earlier from neighbouring Rwanda and Burundi.
Paris urged Washington to drop its reluctance at the Security Council to take part in any force.

"The participation of an American contingent alongside Europeans and Africans would bear witness to the importance the international community attaches to resolving this human tragedy together and...to stability of the African continent," it said.

The United States, wary of getting mired in another ill-fated humanitarian operation like Somalia, said it was still studying whether it could participate and if so, whether with logistics, financial assistance or other means.
France said that scant information about the plight of the refugees in the region was "alarming".

"A large part of them is reported to have dispersed and to be fleeing to the west of Zaire," it said. France said it would earmark an extra 2.6 million francs ($510,000) to relief efforts from a budget for helping refugees.

Meanwhile in Paris, the French branch of the Roman Catholic relief organisation Caritas unloaded almost 40 tonnes of relief supplies from trucks in central Paris to protest at what it called world inaction over the crisis.
"This is a cry of anger," Denis Vienot, head of the group, told France Info radio after the group piled sacks of flour and other supplies at the Trocadero esplanade.
